title: Lunar Night Freeze
text: The Sun has dipped below the lunar horizon. Night has arrived at your Moon base, and it will last for two weeks. Temperatures are plummeting fast!
realFact: A single night on the Moon lasts about 14 Earth days because the Moon rotates very slowly as it orbits our planet.

title: Martian Dust Devil
text: A towering whirlwind of red dust is spinning straight toward your habitat. It kicks sand across your solar panels and rattles the airlock.
realFact: Dust devils on Mars can grow up to 8 kilometers (5 miles) tall, which is five times higher than dust devils on Earth.

title: Solar Flare Incoming
text: The colony orbital satellite detects an intense explosion on the Sun. High-energy radiation waves will strike our base in less than 30 minutes!
realFact: Solar flares shoot radiation into space at the speed of light, reaching planets and moons in mere minutes.

title: Micrometeoroid Hail
text: Tiny space rocks are zipping through the vacuum of space. With no atmosphere to burn them up, they are striking the base's outer hull.
realFact: The Moon has no atmosphere, so even sand-sized micrometeoroids hit the ground traveling faster than a rifle bullet.

title: Earth Communication Delay
text: A life support glitch has popped up! Mission Control on Earth sends advice, but their reply takes nearly twenty minutes to reach your receiver.
realFact: Because Mars is so far away, radio signals can take anywhere from 4 to 24 minutes to travel between Earth and Mars.

title: Abrasive Moon Dust
text: Moon dirt has coated the astronauts' space suits and airlock hinges. The tiny particles are grinding against the rubber seals.
realFact: Lunar dust is extremely sharp like jagged glass because there is no wind or water on the Moon to smooth down the edges.

title: Planet-Wide Mars Dust Storm
text: What started as a small sandstorm has now covered the entire planet of Mars. Dark red clouds have blotted out the Sun for days.
realFact: Mars experiences global dust storms that can shroud the entire world and block over 99% of sunlight from reaching solar panels.

title: Oxygen Scrubber Alarm
text: The machines that remove carbon dioxide from the habitat air are clogged. The crew must clean the filters before the air becomes unsafe.
realFact: Astronauts breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide, which must be constantly scrubbed away to keep the air breathable.

title: Shadowed Lunar Crater Ice
text: A robotic rover discovers frozen water ice hidden inside a dark crater at the Moon's South Pole where the Sun never shines.
realFact: Permanently shadowed craters at the lunar poles can be as cold as -246°C (-410°F), preserving water ice for billions of years.

title: Perchlorates in the Soil
text: Your botany team collects Martian soil to grow fresh crops, but laboratory tests detect toxic salts that must first be washed out.
realFact: Martian soil contains chemical salts called perchlorates that are harmful to humans and must be filtered out before growing food.

title: Galactic Cosmic Ray Burst
text: Deep-space cosmic rays are penetrating through the habitat roof. Astronauts need to retreat into the reinforced storm shelter.
realFact: Galactic cosmic rays are atomic particles shot out by exploding stars outside our solar system.

title: Lunar Noon Heatwave
text: The Sun sits directly overhead in the black sky. With no clouds or atmosphere, the Moon rocks outside have heated up to boiling point!
realFact: During the lunar daytime, surface temperatures can soar above 120°C (250°F), which is hot enough to boil liquid water.

title: Thin Atmosphere Shiver
text: A valve outside your Mars habitat rattles. The Martian air is so thin that sound travels differently and trapped heat escapes quickly into space.
realFact: The air pressure on Mars is less than 1% of Earth's air pressure, making it impossible for humans to breathe without a pressurized suit.

title: Hydroponic Greenhouse Blight
text: A patch of fungus is spreading across the lettuce trays in your hydroponic garden. You need to sanitize the racks before the harvest spoils.
realFact: Plants grown in space need artificial LED lights and careful humidity control because natural soil and fresh rain are unavailable.

title: Solar Conjunction Blackout
text: The Sun moves directly between Earth and your outpost, completely blocking all radio and television transmissions for several days.
realFact: During solar conjunction, charged particles emitted by the Sun disrupt and block all radio communications between Earth and Mars.
